situation (example wording): "How many robberies were there in the US in 2015?", "Murders in Chicago this year", "Robberies with a gun in Atlanta by victim race": any question, typed into one box
what the app does today: The user picks a source tab (or Auto mode, which guesses and asks when unsure); the chosen tab answers even when another source answers better, e.g. NIBRS summing only its reporting agencies for US robberies in 2015.
proposed behavior: The app picks the source for every question: it works out what the question needs (the crime, any detail, the period, the place) and uses the source that actually holds it most completely for that place and period. A source the user asks for in words ("according to NIBRS") is used and labelled, never silently replaced. Where it helps, a button offers the other source's figure. An agency that is in Crime Index but has no figure for the year asked answers a ONE-YEAR question from NIBRS, labelled as the agency's NIBRS report ("Pontiac MI robberies 2024": Crime Index has no 2024 figure; NIBRS has 39), as an agency missing from Crime Index already does. A series never mixes sources (P14): a several-year question keeps one source, with its blank years named (Jeff 2026-11-22: "Answer from NIBRS").
exact default or choices offered: Completed years of the standard (Part I) crimes, clearance and police staffing -> Historical (FBI annual figures; FBI estimates for states and the nation). This year or recent months -> Current Trends. Homicide victim and offender details -> Homicide Reports. Hate crimes -> the Hate Crime file. Details only NIBRS records (victims, offenders, weapons, relationships, locations, property, clearance types) -> NIBRS. An agency missing from Historical, or months no other source holds -> NIBRS, labelled as reporting agencies, never as an estimate.
why: Users cannot be expected to know which source answers a question best; a wrong choice gives a wrong number with the right label. Choosing by what the question needs, and naming the source at the end of the answer, makes answers repeatable and checkable.
status: Decided 2026-10-28 (Jeff: the app picks the source from a single starting page, as the current site does); a blank Crime Index year for one year answers from NIBRS, decided 2026-11-22 (Jeff, through the coordinator: "Answer from NIBRS")
test cases: Tests that cite this row: scripts/test-nibrs-shadow.ts, scripts/test-answer-eval-cases.ts, scripts/test-nibrs-historical.ts.
